detail.allIn: All-in prices, no fees added at checkout.
detail.faqQ1: How does the waiting room work?
detail.faqA1: The waiting room opens 30 minutes before the sale. When the sale opens, everyone inside gets a fair random place in line, so there is no need to click early or refresh.
detail.faqQ2: How many tickets can I buy?
detail.faqA2: Each sale phase has a per-account limit, shown under “Sale phases”.
detail.faqA3: Seats you pick are held for you for 10 minutes while you pay. After that they are released to others.
detail.faqA4: Tickets can't be returned after purchase. If the event is cancelled you are refunded automatically within 7 working days.
detail.notFoundDescription: The event doesn't exist or is no longer on sale.

lab.title: Load lab
lab.description: TicketRush measured under load: a sale opening, thousands of buyers, a webhook storm, a long soak and deliberate faults.
lab.intro: Every number below was measured on the machine listed, as it came out. A budget that was missed says so; what must never be wrong are the invariants: no seat sold twice, no tier sold beyond its capacity.
lab.noResults: No run recorded yet. Run make load-test, then rebuild the page.
lab.scenariosHint: Latency as p50 / p95 / p99. Errors: unexpected answers / rate limited (429).
lab.invariantsHint: No seat with two tickets, no tier beyond capacity, every paid order with exactly its tickets, nobody over the ticket limit, and Redis agreeing with the database. Checked right after the scenario and again once late webhooks, expiries and refunds settled.
lab.soakHint: Memory slope over the last 20 minutes and the Redis hold keys: stable means no steady growth.
lab.broke: What broke and how we fixed it
lab.traceHint: A real trace from Tempo after the run: {spans} spans across {services}, connected from the hold to the email.
